summary: Unix shell interpreter: connecting operating system processes, streams, exit codes, and automating system pipelines.

rows.means: connects standard output (stdout, fd 1) of cmd1 to standard input (stdin) of cmd2
rows.consequence: The fundamental pipeline operator. By default, error messages (stderr, fd 2) do not pass through the pipe, which is why a failing command in the middle of a pipeline can leave you reading an empty result and no error.

rows.means: redirects stdout to file (overwrite) / appends stdout to file
rows.consequence: > truncates the destination file immediately; >> appends new lines to the end of the file.

rows.means: redirects file descriptor 2 (stderr) to file descriptor 1 (stdout)
rows.consequence: cmd > output.log 2>&1 sends both regular output and diagnostic error messages into the same log file.

rows.means: the production safety preamble for all Bash shell scripts
rows.consequence: -e exits immediately on command errors; -u exits on unset variables; -o pipefail catches failures inside piped commands.

rows.means: expands variable / provides fallback if unset or empty
rows.consequence: Always quote variables: "$VAR" prevents whitespace word-splitting and malicious pathname expansion.

rows.means: status code returned by previous command (0 = success, 1-255 = error)
rows.consequence: An exit status of zero means success; any non-zero value is a failure code, which is the opposite of the convention in most languages and the source of a great many inverted conditions.

rows.means: PID of current shell / PID of most recently launched background job
rows.consequence: $$ is often used to generate unique temporary files: /tmp/tempfile.$$.txt.

rows.means: positional argument metadata inside shell scripts and functions
rows.consequence: "$@" preserves exact argument boundary quotes when forwarding arguments to another command.

rows.means: execute cmd2 only if cmd1 succeeded / execute only if cmd1 failed
rows.consequence: mkdir -p dir && cd dir ensures you only change directory if creating it succeeded.

rows.means: tests conditions: -f (file exists), -d (directory), -z (string empty)
rows.consequence: Inside [[ ... ]], modern Bash provides advanced string regex matching (=~) and boolean operators (&&, ||).

rows.means: loops through array elements safely preserving spaces
rows.consequence: Looping without quotes (for x in $items) breaks on filenames containing spaces.

rows.code: while read -r line; do ... done < file.txt
rows.means: reads a file line by line without corrupting backslashes
rows.consequence: The -r flag prevents backslashes from acting as escape characters, preserving exact file contents.

rows.means: marks variable to be inherited by child processes
rows.consequence: Without export, variables are private to the current shell process and invisible to subcommands.

rows.code: chmod +x script.sh and chown user:group file
rows.means: makes file executable / changes user and group ownership
rows.consequence: chmod 755 grants read/write/execute to owner, read/execute to group and others.

rows.means: searches text matching regex recursively with line numbers
rows.consequence: -r searches directories recursively; -n prints line numbers; -i enables case-insensitive matching.

rows.means: stream editor replacing text patterns
rows.consequence: The s command substitutes; the g flag replaces all occurrences across the line rather than just the first.

rows.code: awk '{print $1, $3}' file.txt    # $NF last column, NR line number
rows.means: pattern-directed column processing language
rows.consequence: Splits lines by whitespace by default; $1 is the first column, $NF is the last, and NR is the line number.

rows.means: builds and executes commands from standard input lines
rows.consequence: find . -name "*.tmp" | xargs rm -f deletes all matching files efficiently in batch chunks.

rows.means: registers signals and exit handlers for automatic cleanup
rows.consequence: Ensures temporary directories and locks are removed when the script finishes or is interrupted at the terminal.

rows.means: command substitution: runs command and captures its standard output
rows.consequence: CURRENT_DATE=$(date +%Y-%m-%d) stores the command's terminal output directly into a variable.
